+## #2393 - Example catalog infrastructure (`examples/catalog/<family>/<case>/`, `.camscript`, `xtask catalog`)
+
+- **What was decided:**
+  1. Organize catalog cases under `examples/catalog/<family>/<case>/` with `model/` (generator + mesh), `build.camscript`, `<case>.camproj`, `<case>.nc`, and `README.md`. Seed with `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/` converted from `examples/first-part`, while keeping the legacy `examples/first-part.*` and `examples/models/first-part.obj` paths untouched so release packaging, installer checks, and existing UI/guide tests keep working.
+  2. Bridge `cam.call(tool, args?)` in `crates/app/src/script/` to `crate::mcp::call`, and accept `.camscript` alongside `.js` in `camcraft-cli script`. Every catalog `build.camscript` runs in the Boa JS sandbox over the same `Env` and `History` as MCP and the GUI.
+  3. Add `cargo xtask catalog` (`xtask/src/catalog.rs`, `catalog_media.rs`, `catalog_pdf.rs`) to rebuild or `--check` every case via `camcraft-cli`, render off-screen PNGs into an images-only branch (`catalog-screenshots` by default, refusing `main`/`master`/checked-out/code branches and paths inside the repo tree) via `crates/ui/tests/catalog_render.rs` (with a `--with-guide` hook into #1902's `guide_images` renderer), and optionally build per-case PDFs via `pandoc` + headless Chrome into `target/catalog-pdf/`.
+  4. Pin the catalog in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` (open `<case>.camproj`, force-regenerate all ops, verify clean, post and compare byte-for-byte against `<case>.nc`, and rebuild `build.camscript` end-to-end in a scratch copy), pin `xtask catalog` in `xtask/tests/catalog.rs`, and wire `examples/catalog/` diffs to `app:example_catalog` via `xtask/src/catalog.rs::map_catalog` called from `xtask/src/quick.rs`.
+
+- **Why:**
+  - Bridging `cam.call` directly to `mcp::call` gives `.camscript` immediate access to all undoable commands (`set_stock`, `add_tool`, `add_operation`, `edit_operation`, `set_wcs`, `load_machine`, etc.) over one shared `Env` and `History` instead of duplicating command wrappers in `script/api.rs`.
+  - Committing rendered PNGs via an isolated temporary index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` + `hash-object` / `write-tree` / `commit-tree`) updates the images-only branch without ever touching the working tree or risking screenshots landing in the product branch.
+  - Keeping `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` as the output posted by current `upstream/main` avoids mixing legacy v59 `.nc` text with current generator output.
+
+- **Considered and dropped:**
+  - Defining a custom line-based verb parser separate from Boa JS `cam`: creates a second scripting dialect to maintain and diverges from `camcraft-cli script` / `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts`.
+  - Moving or deleting `examples/first-part.camproj`: would break `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `scripts/installer.ps1`, `xtask/src/release_tests.rs`, `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_images.rs`, and `site/content/guide/automate/cli.md`.
+  - Putting `camcraft-app` as a dependency of `xtask`: violates workspace layering and slows `xtask` builds; invoking the built `camcraft-cli` binary keeps `xtask` dependency-light and tests the real shipped CLI.
+
+- **Cost to change later:** Low — `cam.call` is a single table entry in `VERBS`, `examples/catalog/` discovery is filesystem-driven, and `xtask catalog` subcommands/flags are self-contained in `xtask/src/catalog*.rs`.

+# First Part (2D Face, 2D Pocket, Drill)
+
+A 100 x 60 x 15 mm clean-room aluminum test plate machined from a 100 x 60 x 20 mm box stock.
+
+## What it shows
+
+1. **Face (`Face1`, `EM-1000-4FL`):** Faces the top 5 mm off the 20 mm stock down to `Z15` (top of the central island).
+2. **2D Pocket (`2D Pocket1`, `EM-0600-4FL`):** Clears the 5 mm shelf around the 60 x 30 mm central island with a helical ramp entry down to `Z10`.
+3. **Drill (`Drill1`, `DR-0600`):** Drills four 6 mm through-holes around the flange at `(±38, ±23)` using `G73` peck drilling (`Fanuc` built-in post).
+
+## Files
+
+- `model/gen_first_part_obj.py` — parametric watertight voxel-CSG generator for the test solid.
+- `model/first-part.obj` — generated quad mesh imported by `build.camscript`.
+- `build.camscript` — headless script building `first-part.camproj` and posting `first-part.nc` through CamCraft's undoable commands.
+- `first-part.camproj` — committed project with generated toolpaths.
+- `first-part.nc` — committed Fanuc NC program verified byte-for-byte in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.
+
+## Rebuild and verify
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/first-part
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog
+```

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regenerate first-part.obj, the fixture model for the docs example project.
+
+The part is a clean-room Camcraft fixture: a 100 x 60 x 10 mm flange with a
+60 x 30 mm central island rising to z = 15, and four through-bores about
+(+/-38, +/-23). The bores are 6.4 mm squares - the machined envelope of
+the drill op's 6 mm round holes with 0.2 mm clearance - because Camcraft's
+verify gate compares the program's cut volume to the model solid, so the
+model must already carry the holes' voids.
+
+Method: the solid is exactly a union of boxes whose faces all sit on one
+plane set (x: +/-30, +/-34.8, +/-41.2, +/-50; y: +/-15, +/-19.8,
++/-26.2, +/-30; z: 0, 10, 15), so the boundary can be built exactly by
+voxel CSG over that grid: every inside/outside cell face is emitted as a
+unit quad. Unit quads tile every plane the same way from both sides, so
+the mesh is conforming (no T-junctions), watertight, and consistently
+outward-oriented; the script self-checks that before writing.
+
+Usage: python gen_first_part_obj.py [output.obj]
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+FLANGE = (-50.0, 50.0, -30.0, 30.0, 0.0, 10.0)   # x0 x1 y0 y1 z0 z1
+ISLAND = (-30.0, 30.0, -15.0, 15.0, 10.0, 15.0)
+BORE_HALF = 3.2  # 6 mm hole radius plus 0.2 mm envelope clearance
+BORE_XY = [(38.0, 23.0), (-38.0, 23.0), (38.0, -23.0), (-38.0, -23.0)]
+
+XS = sorted({-50.0, -41.2, -34.8, -30.0, 30.0, 34.8, 41.2, 50.0})
+YS = sorted({-30.0, -26.2, -19.8, -15.0, 15.0, 19.8, 26.2, 30.0})
+ZS = [0.0, 10.0, 15.0]
+PLANES = [XS, YS, ZS]
+
+
+def inside_box(p, box):
+    x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1 = box
+    return x0 <= p[0] <= x1 and y0 <= p[1] <= y1 and z0 <= p[2] <= z1
+
+
+def in_bore(p):
+    if not (0.0 <= p[2] <= 10.0):
+        return False
+    return any(abs(p[0] - cx) <= BORE_HALF and abs(p[1] - cy) <= BORE_HALF
+               for cx, cy in BORE_XY)
+
+
+def solid(p):
+    return (inside_box(p, FLANGE) or inside_box(p, ISLAND)) and not in_bore(p)
+
+
+def build():
+    dims = [len(p) - 1 for p in PLANES]
+    inside = set()
+    for i in range(dims[0]):
+        for j in range(dims[1]):
+            for k in range(dims[2]):
+                mid = [(PLANES[a][idx] + PLANES[a][idx + 1]) / 2
+                       for a, idx in enumerate((i, j, k))]
+                if solid(tuple(mid)):
+                    inside.add((i, j, k))
+
+    groups = {}
+    for cell in inside:
+        for axis in range(3):
+            for sign in (+1, -1):
+                nxt = list(cell)
+                nxt[axis] += sign
+                if tuple(nxt) in inside:
+                    continue
+                plane = cell[axis] + (1 if sign > 0 else 0)
+                a, b = (d for d in range(3) if d != axis)
+                groups.setdefault((axis, plane, sign, a, b), set()).add(
+                    (cell[a], cell[b]))
+
+    # with a, b the other two axes in ascending order, walking (a then b)
+    # gives a normal of +axis for axis 0 and 2 and -axis for axis 1
+    # (hat{x} x hat{z} = -hat{y}), so check that sign before emitting
+    WALK_SIGN = {0: +1, 1: -1, 2: +1}
+    quads = []  # each a list of 4 (x, y, z) coordinate tuples, oriented
+    for (axis, plane, sign, a, b), cells in groups.items():
+        for (ca, cb) in sorted(cells):  # unit quads tile each plane exactly,
+            quad = []                   # from both sides, so no T-junctions
+            for p, q in [(ca, cb), (ca + 1, cb), (ca + 1, cb + 1), (ca, cb + 1)]:
+                pos = [None, None, None]
+                pos[axis] = PLANES[axis][plane]
+                pos[a] = PLANES[a][p]
+                pos[b] = PLANES[b][q]
+                quad.append(tuple(pos))
+            if WALK_SIGN[axis] != sign:
+                quad.reverse()
+            quads.append(quad)
+    return quads
+
+
+def check(quads):
+    """Watertight and consistently oriented: every directed edge appears
+    exactly once and its reverse appears exactly once."""
+    seen = {}
+    for quad in quads:
+        for p, q in zip(quad, quad[1:] + quad[:1]):
+            if p == q:
+                raise SystemExit("degenerate quad: %r" % (quad,))
+            if (p, q) in seen:
+                raise SystemExit("directed edge reused: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+            seen[(p, q)] = True
+    for (p, q) in seen:
+        if (q, p) not in seen:
+            raise SystemExit("open edge: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+
+
+def main():
+    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "first-part.obj"
+    quads = build()
+    check(quads)
+
+    vid = {}
+    vlines = []
+    for quad in quads:
+        for p in quad:
+            if p not in vid:
+                vid[p] = len(vlines) + 1
+                vlines.append("v %g %g %g" % p)
+    flines = []
+    for quad in quads:
+        flines.append("f " + " ".join(str(vid[p]) for p in quad))
+
+    with open(out, "w") as fh:
+        fh.write(HEADER)
+        fh.write("\n" + "\n".join(vlines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(flines) + "\n")
+    print("wrote %s: %d vertices, %d faces" % (out, len(vlines), len(flines)))
+
+
+HEADER = """\
+# Camcraft docs example: "first part" - a 100 x 60 x 15 mm plate with a
+# 5 mm shelf milled around a 60 x 30 mm central island and four 6.4 mm
+# square through-bores about (+/-38, +/-23): the machined envelope of the
+# drill op's 6 mm round holes, 0.2 mm clearance. The verify gate judges
+# the program against the model solid, so the model carries the holes'
+# voids. Authored for this repository (clean-room fixture); generated by
+# gen_first_part_obj.py, this watertight quad mesh is what the example
+# project embeds as facets."""
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# CamCraft Example Catalog
+
+Reproducible, regression-tested CAM projects organized by operation family (`examples/catalog/<family>/<case>/`).
+
+## Case layout
+
+Every case folder `<family>/<case>/` contains:
+
+- `model/` — clean-room geometry generator script and generated mesh (`.obj`, `.stl`, or `.step`).
+- `build.camscript` — headless CamCraft script (`camcraft-cli script build.camscript` from the case directory) that creates the document via undoable commands, generates, verifies, saves `<case>.camproj`, and posts `<case>.nc`.
+- `<case>.camproj` — committed project file.
+- `<case>.nc` — committed NC program.
+- `README.md` — what the case shows, its operations/tools, and what to inspect.
+
+## Adding a new case
+
+1. Copy the seed case folder `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/` to `examples/catalog/<family>/<case>/`.
+2. Replace `model/` with your clean-room model generator and mesh.
+3. Update `build.camscript` and `README.md`, naming `<case>.camproj` and `<case>.nc`.
+4. Rebuild the case's `.camproj` and `.nc` from `build.camscript`:
+   ```sh
+   cargo xtask catalog --case <family>/<case>
+   ```
+5. Verify the catalog test suite passes:
+   ```sh
+   cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog
+   ```
+
+## Catalog commands
+
+- `cargo xtask catalog` — rebuild every case's `<case>.camproj` and `<case>.nc` from its `build.camscript`.
+- `cargo xtask catalog --check` — verify all case layouts and check that every `build.camscript` reproduces the committed `<case>.nc` without modifying tracked files.
+- `cargo xtask catalog --screenshots` — render off-screen PNG screenshots via `camcraft-ui` into an images-only branch (`catalog-screenshots` by default, never into the product tree).
+- `cargo xtask catalog --pdf` — build per-case PDFs into `target/catalog-pdf/` using `pandoc` and headless Chrome.
